questions.solution:

salary reduced = 40%

salary increased = 40%

After reduction = 100 - (40/100) ×100 = 60% 

Taking the reduced salary for increament

questions.question:
If 5A = 6B and 6A = 4C, the ratio of B : C is:

A. 4 : 3

B. 5 : 6

C. 5 : 9

D. 10 : 15

5A = 6B and 6A = 4C

**Concept used:**

Ratio method use

5A = 6B

⇒ A/B = 6/5 ----(1)

6A = 4C

⇒ A/C = 4/6 = 2/3

⇒ C/A = 3/2 ----(2)

Multiplying (1) and (2) get,

(A/B) × (C/A) = (6/5) × (3/2)

⇒ C/B = 9/5

⇒ B/C = 5/9

⇒ B : C = 5 : 9

**∴****The ratio of B : C is 5 : 9. **

Find the compound interest of Rs 30,000 for 2 years 73 days at the rate of 35/4% per annum.

C. Rs. 6101

D. Rs. 3635
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs. 30,000

Time = 2 years 73 days

Rate = 35/4% per annum

**Concept Used:**

Interest on the interest is known as compound interest

**Formula Used:**

Amount = Principal + Interest

For Compound Interest

Amount = Principal[1 + Rate/100]Time 

For Simple Interest 

Interest = Principal × Rate/100 × Time

**Calculation:**

Time = 2 years 73 days

Converting it into years

⇒ 2 years + 73/365 years

⇒ 2 + 1/5 years

Now, we are calculating compound interest for 2 years 

Amount = Rs. 30,000[1 + 35/400]² 

⇒ Amount = Rs. 30,000[1 + 7/80]² 

⇒ Amount = Rs. 30,000[87/80]² 

⇒ Amount = Rs. 30,000 × 87/80 × 87/80

⇒ Amount = Rs. 35,479.7

The Amount is principal for the 1/5 year

Interest = Rs. 35,479.7 × 35/400 × 1/5

⇒ Interest = Rs. 620.9

Compound interest of 2 years = Rs. 35,479.7 – Rs. 30,000

⇒ Rs. 5,479.7

Compound interest of Rs. 30,000 in 2 years and 73 days = Compound interest of 2 years + interest of 1/5 year

⇒ Rs. 5,479.7 + Rs. 620.9

⇒ Rs. 6,100.6 ≈ Rs. 6,101

**∴ The compound interest of Rs. 30,000 for 2 years 73 days at the rate of 35/4% per annum is Rs. 6,101**

questions.question:
What is not true with data conversion?

A. Upgrading from one version to another version

B. Receiving data from a legacy system

C. Receiving data from another module

D. It may use a standard import program
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Upgrading from one version to another version.**__

__
 
• Converting data into formats that help you understand, analyze, and present information is required in all fields of work.
 
 
• **Viewing data in a different format** can help to unlock new insights that may otherwise go unnoticed.
 
• While data isn’t necessarily “hidden” in any format, by converting and restructuring data into something new, you often are exposed to the equivalent of a new perspective.
 
• It is this unique **perspective that can give you a better** and more well-rounded understanding of the data you have.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Data conversion is widely used for reasons related to accessibility. Often data is stored in a specific file format that only certain software can access and read.
 
• This is **due to the innate structure of the file itself**. While this was once a limitation, there are now many strategies for converting data that allow for greater flexibility and enable you to use the data in any way you’d like.
 
• With more and more data being collected, it is inevitable that **data conversion will be a task that you complete, no matter how simple or complex the conversion.**

questions.question:
The most important component of glass is ______.

C. Silica

D. Sodium Borate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Silica.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Glass is made from **silicon, which is the second most common element in Earth's crust. **
 
• The main constituent of glass is silicon dioxide (SiO 2).
 
 
• The most common form of **silica used in glassmaking has always been sand**.
 
 
 
• Glass is a translucent object.
 
• Glass is a** significant material used in lightbulbs.**
 
• Glass is made from natural and abundant raw materials (sand, soda ash and limestone) that are melted at very high temperatures to form a new material: glass.
 
• At high-temperature glass is structurally similar to liquids, however, at ambient temperature, it behaves like solids.
 
• As a result, glass can be poured, blown, press and moulded into plenty of shapes.
